To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a pool of the renal Na(+)-K-Cl- cotransporters NKCC2 and NCC are present in cholesterol-en rich lipid rafts (LRR).
NKCC2 is a lipid raft-associated protein that is regulated by vasopressin in a cholesterol-dependent manner.

a pool of the renal Na(+)-K+-Cl- co-transporter (NKCC2) is present in cholesterol-en rich lipid rafts and that these rafts are required for the activity of NKCC2 and the AVP-mediated trafficking of the transporter to the plasma membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and physiological mechanisms that control NaCl reabsorption in the renal TAL.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the surface expression of the renal Na(+)-K+-2Cl(-) transporter NKCC2, which is responsible for transepithelial sodium chloride reabsorption in the kidney.
the role of LR in the regulation of NKCC2 activity and trafficking.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LR are involved in the regulation of NKCC2 activity and AVP-induced surface trafficking.
NKCC2 is a lipid-raft-associated protein, and that the lipid rafts play an important role in the regulation of NKCC2 activity and trafficking.
NKCC2 is present in lipid rafts, and that these are important for its trafficking.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LR are involved in the regulation of Na+ and Cl- reabsorption in the TAL of the loop of henle.
NKCC2 is an LR-associated protein and AVP-induced NKCC2 trafficking in TAL cells is LR-dependent.
the LR is a critical membrane domain for the regulation of NKCC2 function and trafficking.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LR are involved in the regulation of NKCC2 surface trafficking, activity, and transepithelial transport in the kidney.
NKCC2 is present in LR, which are cholesterol-enriched microdomains of the plasma membrane and endomembrane system.
